classification.difficultyReason: Identify the common chord endpoints for two obtuse circumference angles despite the extra radii, then equate the angles on the same arc.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.sourceRegion: Third row, middle column, part aaa
spec.description: Four circumference points form crossed chords. The upper-left and lower-left interior angles both stand on the arc between the top and bottom points on the right of the circle. A leader identifies the upper-left interior angle as 130 degrees. Radii join centre O to the top and bottom points. Ordinary source colours are replaced with black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The two circumference angles stand on the same arc, so x equals 130 degrees. The top and bottom points are joined to O by radii, not by a diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 130-degree angle, centre label O and unknown x are visible; the supplied answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
Angles at the circumference standing on the same arc are equal.
$$x=130^\circ$$
